evidence: Reachability: every capability is reachable. Runtime: environment/Dockerfile installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, matching instruction.md:13 'Server dependencies are already available' and integration.md ('Node 22 ... Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH'). tests/test.sh:96-111 launches node /app/server.js (or the writable copy) with env -i PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT=3000/DB_PATH, exactly what hireops_rules.md section 8 and instruction.md:13 tell the builder to expect; /app is a git-initialised writable workspace. Seed: seed_data.json provides all 10 accounts named at instruction.md:17 with roles, 3 jobs with interview_limit, 16 applications with stage/position (APP-301 carries rejected_from/reject_reason), 127 messages (APP-101 has 120 = the 'long' conversation), 3 notes, 6 read markers, candidate_status_labels identical to the rules section 7 table, thread_page_size 30. The password is stated (instruction.md:17), so the seed needs no hashes. Facts the criteria check against the seed can be derived from it: Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 of 3 APP-301 messages, and the third is by USR-REC3, so 1 unread, which matches functional prompt step Z. Platform Engineer Applied order Greta/Ade/Marco and Screen order Priya/Samuel match positions. Noor's APP-101 note text matches. Network is public (task.toml network_mode public; instruction.md:13 lets the browser use a CDN and forbids only an outside data service). The SKILL delivery profile makes the public-network wording authoritative over the Internal Quality Checks sheet's 'no network' annotation for row 6. Either way the server needs no network, so the conflict is moot here. The golden is evidence that the work can be done: the scripted golden observations (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json, hash-verified against raw-evidence-index.json, NOT a configured judge run) pass all listed groups, including stale-move naming, bulk/undo, unread/seen, paging and live arrival at 802 ms. Single reading: I checked each graded rule for a second reasonable reading against the exact functional-protocol scenario. (a) Undo 'back ... at the place it came from' could mean an absolute index or a position relative to neighbours. In protocol B both readings give the same result: V returns to the top of Applied; Y,W,X return ahead of Z,A2 in Applied, read as Y,W,X,Z,A2; A2 returns to an empty Applied. So the ambiguity is not graded. (b) Undo history: someone could implement a stack, where the previous move becomes undoable after an undo. hireops_rules.md:116-117 rules that out ('A move can be undone once; an undo cannot itself be undone, and an earlier move is no longer undoable once the same person has made a later one'). This is what hro_undo_once grades (Z stays in Screen). (c) 'nobody has touched those cards' (instruction.md:3) could include notes. rules:116 defines it ('Adding a note does not count as a change'), and hro_undo_restores matches that. (d) Is reopening an undoable move? rules:114 ('restores a rejection reason that the move removed') makes it one, which matches hro_reopen. (e) Stale detection: a design keyed on the from-stage would accept protocol C's A-B-A replay. rules:94 says 'Every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves', so that design does not conform. One reading. (f) Bulk ordering: rules:107-108 define board order (stage order, then place), which matches hro_bulk_move (A2, V). Interview places are counted for the whole set. (g) Hiring-manager limits: rules:87-89 make Interview->Screen and rejecting from Screen refused. Opening jobs is refused ('Only a recruiter opens a job'), and adding candidates is a recruiter role in the role table and section 2. This matches hro_mgr_early_refused. (h) Access status codes: rules:38-40 give 401 for anonymous callers, 403 for a role that does not reach an action, and 404 for a candidate asking about someone else's application. hro_anonymous requires 401, and hro_candidate_private requires 'not found'. Both match. (i) Unread for a conversation never opened: rules:168-170 counts every message by others. The graded checks use deltas or a sequence the judge observes, so either reading passes. (j) Job validation: places must be a whole number from 1 to 50 (rules:45). A blank title being refused follows from 'A job has a title' and is a reasonable single reading. Ungraded ambiguities, recorded for completeness and not defects for this row: whether a hiring manager may read other jobs' boards, notes or Activity; whether a re-order counts as an undoable move; how a bulk move to Rejected collects its reason; and whether a card already in the target stage may join a bulk move. No criterion depends on any of these. Where a criterion touches one, it accepts either reading (hro_mgr_other_job and hro_notes allow 'not offered or refused'). Cross-row observation (outside row 6; route to criterion/protocol-feasibility rows, not a row-6 defect): in protocol U, hro_seen expects Rafael's new message to show 'not seen' until 'Tomas opens it'. If the judge leaves Tomas's independent context open on that conversation at the newest message, a conforming app has to mark the message seen on arrival (rules:175 'if they are at the newest message, it is shown and counts as read'). The golden does this too (solution/app/public/js/threads.js:157 'if (stay) { toBottom(); paint(c); if (theirs && active) markRead(id); }'), so hro_seen would then fail even a correct app. The functional prompt.md:11 tells the judge to close each independent context after use, which mitigates this, but step U never explicitly says to close or leave Tomas's conversation before Rafael sends. No configured judge run was available to measure it. Suggested to the owner: say in that U step that Tomas's conversation is closed or left before Rafael sends. Runtime note: no configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists. This row is a source-level judgement, supported by the hash-verified scripted golden observations only.
